subject: Procurement readiness + commercial path for Acme Retail
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + procurement questions (Acme Retail)

Hey Jason / Samir - great talk earlier today, thanks for the time. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can align the commercial path before we get procurement involved. Attaching a high-level pricing packet and a procurement checklist for your finance team.

Key takeaways (from call):
- Primary use case: in-product recommendations & personalized search, initial pilot hitting ~5M tokens/month.
- Timing: pilot target kickoff in April, production in Q3 if pilot passes SLOs.
- Preference: start with Hosted API to iterate quickly; we discussed Dedicated for predictable throughput once we scale.

Questions for procurement readiness (high level):
1) Paper process: do you require an MSA + SOW before procurement issues a PO, or can we proceed with a standard order form + PO?
2) Payment method: does Acme prefer card for early pilots and PO/invoice for contracts over a threshold? If PO, are net30 or net45 terms standard?
3) Marketplace interest: would you prefer to transact via AWS Marketplace (for faster internal approval) or direct Redwood invoice?
4) Approvals: who in your procurement/finance org needs the commercial summary (legal, procurement, finance contact names/emails would be helpful).

Commercial notes (brief):
- Hosted API: usage-based; can do monthly invoicing by PO for larger pilots (we can accept PO > $5k/month with net30 depending on legal).
- Dedicated: reserved capacity with commits; typically 12-month term with monthly invoices tied to commit; requires MSA + SOW.
- Private: customer-managed deployment; involves license + platform fee, longer procurement cycle and legal review.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm procurement path (PO vs card vs marketplace) and point of contact.
- We provide a 1-page commercial summary & SOW draft for procurement review.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-v1.pdf, procurement-checklist.xlsx

Thanks - I'll loop Aditya on the next note to call out the packaging/pricing options to share with procurement.

Best,
Marissa

From: Jason Lee <jason.lee@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-retail.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T17:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + procurement questions (Acme Retail)

Thanks Marissa - useful recap. A few answers from procurement/finance perspective:

1) Paper process: For pilots under $50k we typically can proceed with an order form + PO. For anything involving dedicated/commits or a platform/license we will need an MSA + SOW.
2) Payment method: Finance prefers to use PO/invoice when the annual spend is expected to exceed $25k; otherwise card for pilots is fine. Net30 is our standard on POs.
3) Marketplace: AWS Marketplace is preferred by our procurement team since it accelerates approvals and simplifies invoicing. If Redwood can offer the same SKU on AWS Marketplace, that would be ideal.
4) Approvals: Please send a short commercial summary to me and I'll route it to procurement (Emily Tran - emily.tran@acme-retail.com) and legal (Tom Reyes - tom.reyes@acme-retail.com).

For the pilot, we're leaning Hosted to start; if performance looks good and costs stabilize we'll evaluate Dedicated for Q3. Can you include a clear mapping of Hosted vs Dedicated pricing (committed monthly spend and expected latency/cost tradeoffs) in the one-pager? Also include estimated lead times for Dedicated and any Marketplace listing timelines.

Appreciate it - will wait for the one-pager and SOW draft.

- Jason
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + procurement questions (Acme Retail)

Jason - great, thanks for the clarity. See answers inline below and next steps.

On 2026-03-18 at 17:46, Jason Lee wrote:
> For the pilot, we're leaning Hosted to start; if performance looks good and costs stabilize we'll evaluate Dedicated for Q3. Can you include a clear mapping of Hosted vs Dedicated pricing (committed monthly spend and expected latency/cost tradeoffs) in the one-pager? Also include estimated lead times for Dedicated and any Marketplace listing timelines.

Yes - we'll deliver a one-page commercial summary that includes:
- Hosted (on our hosted API): usage-based billing, card for small pilots or monthly invoicing by PO for larger pilots. Typical recommendation: pilot on Hosted with an optional monthly commit (e.g., 2-3k USD/month commit) to get discounted unit pricing without locking to Dedicated.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): 12-month commit is typical; monthly invoiced against the commit with PO; lead time 4-8 weeks depending on region & GPU availability.
- Private deployment: longer procurement / legal lead time; generally not recommended for pilot phase.

Marketplace note: we are live on AWS Marketplace but not every SKU is listed. For faster procurement via Marketplace we can prioritize listing the Hosted SKU for your pilot; timeline is typically 2-3 weeks once procurement/legal content is finalized.

I'll attach an updated one-pager and a short SOW draft for a Hosted pilot that supports PO invoicing. Aditya - can you confirm the recommended commit thresholds and discount bands we should show for a ~5M tokens/month pilot?

Next steps:
- We'll send the one-pager + SOW draft to you and Emily/ Tom for procurement/legal review.
- If Marketplace is preferred, we'll surface the Marketplace path in the SOW and prioritization plan.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: sow-draft.docx
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Lee <jason.lee@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2026-03-19T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + procurement questions (Acme Retail)

Quick commercial note - adding for clarity so procurement sees concrete numbers in the one-pager:

For ~5M tokens/month pilot (expected mix of generations + embeddings):
- Hosted (on-demand): ~$3,000-4,500/month (pay-as-you-go); unit costs higher but zero lead time.
- Hosted (small commit): 2,500 USD/month commit -> ~15-20% unit discount vs on-demand. We can accept POs for commits >= $2,500/month with net30 after MSA/order form.
- Dedicated (reserved, 12-mo): typical entry point ~12k-18k USD/month commit depending on GPU profile; provides 40-55% lower unit cost for steady-state workloads. Requires MSA + SOW and ~4-8 week provisioning.

Marketplace: listing the Hosted pilot SKU is usually 2-3 weeks after we turn over commercial/legal artifacts. If Acme prefers Marketplace, we can prioritize that to shorten procurement friction.

I'll add these numbers to the one-pager and label which path is recommended for a pilot vs production ramp.

- Aditya
